newsitem.title: UK: Lex sells 17 dealerships to Pendragon.
newsitem.headline: Lex sells 17 dealerships to Pendragon.

text.p: Britain's Pendragon Plc said on Friday it was acquiring 17 dealership from vehicle leasing company Lex Service Plc for 44 million pounds ($73.5 million).

At the same time Lex reported pre-tax profits before exceptional items of 30.4 million pounds in the six months to June 30, up from 27.7 million pounds in the same period a year ago. It proposed an interim dividend of 6.8 pence a share, up from 6.4 pence.

"We have made an important strategic move which will focus Lex Retail on fewer, specialist, manufacturers where we have a good track record of performance," Andy Harrison, Lex's chief executive, said in a statement. "This is a core business which we intend to develop".
Pendragon said in its statement its expansion of major market areas with Ford and Vauxhall includes plans for a further 30 franchise points at a total investment of 64 million pounds.

To help strengthen its balance sheet for these developments, Pendragon said it was seeking to raise around 56 million pounds in a four-for-seven rights issue of just over 22 million shares at 265 pence a share.
"The acquisition from Lex and the new development significantly expand Pendragon's relationships within the volume sector of the market," said Pendragon's chief executive Trevor Finn.
"The move towards large franchise territories will result in significant economies of scale and we now have the financial resources to develop fully these new opportunities".
Shares in Pendragon were down 32 pence at 316-1/2 pence while those for Lex were 11 pence higher at 411-1/2 pence. ($ = 0.598 British Pounds)
